True Name: The name of a thing in the Old Speech; knowing it confers power
Old Speech: The language of the Making, in which things cannot be lied about
Equilibrium: The cosmic balance that magic either honors or transgresses
Shadow (Earthsea sense): The exiled part of self that must be named and integrated
Nameless Ones: The chthonic powers older than the True Name system
Hainish cycle: The interconnected SF setting of multiple-branch humanity
Kemmer: The periodic sexual state of Gethenians
Necessary suffering: Le Guin's explicit distinction between suffering that serves growth and suffering that is merely imposed
Prose compression: The virtue of cutting to what the sentence actually requires
True speech / true listening: Le Guin's dual craft — saying what is and hearing what is
Carrier-bag theory: Le Guin's model of narrative as container (harvest, accumulate) vs spear (hero, pierce)
